draft.title: Taxation without representation
card: Colonists were British subjects, but they elected no members to the British Parliament in London. They did elect their own colonial assemblies.
The Stamp Act of 1765 taxed printed items such as newspapers, legal papers and playing cards. It was passed by Parliament to raise money from the colonies.
Many colonists said only their own assemblies had the right to tax them. They argued that a tax passed by a body they had no say in broke the rights of British subjects.
The complaint was about who made the decision, not only about the cost. Colonists organised protests and boycotts, and Parliament repealed the Stamp Act in 1766.
draft.remember: The objection was to being taxed by a parliament where colonists had no vote or members.

a.q: What was the main objection colonists made to the Stamp Act?
opts: It was a tax made by a parliament they did not sit in
It was a tax that was too high for any colonist to pay
It was a tax made by their own colonial assemblies
It was a tax that only applied to British-born colonists
a.why: Colonists argued that only their own assemblies could tax them, and the Stamp Act came from Parliament in London, where they had no members. The cost mattered, but the main complaint was about who had the right to impose the tax.
a.clue: Think about who passed the tax, not how much it cost.

b.q: Daniel, a printer in Boston in 1765, says: 'I would pay this tax gladly if my own assembly had voted for it.' What does his view show?
opts: His objection is to who made the tax, not to the tax itself
His objection is to the price of paper, not who passed the tax
He supports Parliament's right to tax the colonies directly
He opposes all taxes of any kind, whoever passes them
b.why: Daniel accepts a tax passed by his own assembly, so his complaint is about who has the authority to tax him. This matches the colonial argument. It is not a rejection of all taxes, and he does not accept Parliament's right to tax the colonies.
b.clue: He would accept the same tax if a different body passed it.
